Stevens has been one of the most considerate and caring professors I have had since being in school. She's completely understanding and funny!! I had her for two classes and looked forward to them all the time. Truly one of the best.
I literally love her to bits. She made me remember why I even liked English, and Im an ENGINEERING student. I wish I could've minored in it...

Amazing professor, one of the best I've had at UIUC. Her lectures are very funny and she puts a lot of work into engaging the students. She picks very interesting texts for the class and gives great feedback. Very fair grading. If you show effort, come to class and submit all assignments, you will get an A in the class.

Amazing lectures and great sense of humor. It helps if you're interested in it but she's so fun regardless. Always fun to discuss with and have fun creative assignments. She really cares about what she teaches and it shows.

Although he has an impressive educational background, I'm skeptical of what he actually knows.

This professor flies by the seat of his pants, he changes the syllabus as he pleases, there is no consistency in expectations, he changes, adds, and drops major assignments all of the time and changed the weightings of exams midsemester. He is also vindictive, he asks for feedback and if you give any sense of negative feedback, he will get angry.

He clearly wrote his own RMP when he was at Mizzou. If you like nuclear you need to tough it out for his classes. Good luck.

The class is not too difficult, but he curved our class down. His assignments  may have you do unrelated computer projects that are graded incredibly harshly. His schedule is inconsistent with the syllabus, and he does not reply to emails.

ACCY 517 & Adel are the hardest class I have ever taken, including FIN 300.  I have learned so much from ACCY 517 and it is the most beneficial class I have ever taken in my collegiate career.  He pours his passion into the subject, he slows the class down when students don't understand, he holds tons of office hours to help.

Be prepared to show up to all lectures, but he's such a knowledgeable and charismatic instructor that this won't be hard.

If you have the opportunity to take a class with Ali, do it. "ok" is the first word I can think of to describe. I went to Paul Kwiat's lectures a couple of times and he was more enthusiastic about the material and had more understandable explanations. Prof Abdu cares about his students! Really great experience taking the course with him! Even though the exams and home works were tough, prof Abdu is one of the best professors I've ever had.

Class felt unorganized and didn't follow the syllabus, making it hard to prepare for lectures. Exams focused on random details instead of what was taught. TAs did most of the real teaching, and the professor missed classes often. Hard class already, but the teaching style made it much worse.

review_highlights.comment: HK207 is a great course to take to fill a quant 1; it's not hard at all for anyone with even the most basic math background. Watch all the lectures on 2x speed, and do all the discussion posts at once, and then respond later. Makes workload much easier. Midterm was open, so was the final, both extremely simple. Great Class for a tough credit.

Easy A online class, but the workload was a lot for 2 credit hours. Homework consisted of chapter reading, 1 discussion post on a 30 min-2 hour documentary, 2 peer responses, and a quiz/short project. Course lasted 8 weeks and 8 modules with 2 exams (no final cumulative). Lots of opportunities for extra credit. Overall, it was a solid class.

There are a lot of weekly assignments in this class. A discussion post, two reply posts (400 words and 250 words), a quiz and all the readings. You also sometimes have to watch lengthy documentaries to be prepared for the discussion (usually interesting and on Netflix). Overall would give this class a 3/5. It's not bad, but not my favorite.

Was an easy class for 2.0 credits. Online so submit the work on your own time by Sunday, and it is eight weeks, and the course itself is not too demanding. But be prepared it is a lot of movie-watching paired with discussion posts. There is one project, a midterm and a final, and quizzes so a lot of test material. Overall a great course!

I really like her, this class would have been much better if it were in person because online was kind of difficult- there was a movie to watch almost every week with a 400 word discussion post plus two 250 word discussion replies due on Wednesday (400) and Friday (replies)

Farina is very engaging in lectures and extremely friendly. He stays after class to answer as many questions as possible. He is also very friendly outside of class if you see him on campus. Despite being new here, he seems to be settled in very nicely on campus and would 100% recommend taking his class.

Farina is great. Lectures are hilarious with him, and he is great. If you have questions, he is accessible after class to answer any questions and genuinely cares about you. He just joined the Physics Department here this year, which is why there's not a lot of ratings for him.

Professor Farina is awesome! His lectures are really fun and he has a talent for explaining things. He is also hilarious during the lecture and very accessible outside of class. He really cares about his students doing well. Definitely one of the best professors I've had here.

analysis.name: Jacob Fredericks
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He does not try to give credit on assignments. If you are somewhat wrong, you're getting many points off. He likes to hear himself talk. He will repeat himself over and over as if you are in grade school. He seems power hungry and he wants you to call him "doctor". Least favorite by far.

This was an easy A of a course. Only a brief discussion post, a 300-500 word paper, a 5 question quiz, and some reading each week. Probably the easiest course I've taken. Dr. Fredericks also put effort to make it that way, he explained a lot through email and was very accessible. Although its an online class, he makes the class better.

Asynchronous online class. There's a weekly narrative paper (at least 250 words), a quiz based on the readings (provided to you, no need to buy a textbook), and a discussion post with at least 4 replies on the Packback platform, and a final paper (at least 500 words). As long as you follow all instructions, you should get an A in this class.

Made us pay a $40 Packback fee to "get access to the full platform", then micromanaged every single sentence that we could write. PB is already ridiculous, and if you're not going to give creative liberty for us to "earn" the curiosity points, then why use it in the first place? Overall, really overbearing and slightly pretentious.

If you're looking for an easy A, this class is it.  The homework takes a long time, but it was easy.  He's not as bad as the comments say he is.  Just remember to not miss a single deadline, and follow his instructions properly. He is strict, but if you do what you're told, you can get away with a high A or A+.

analysis.name: Felix Leditzky
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: 257 is awfully designed due to the course design. As a lecturer Felix was great, and I would have given him a 5 if it was for a different course. He is a very smart guy and always helping out on the course forum. Only complaint is he scrolled through notes fast, but lectures and notes were recorded.  Would 100% recommend him for another course.

** FOR MATH257 **
This class just tries to do too much with all the coding plus teaching basic linear algebra. You are completely on your own for all of the Python, and only left with lectures for concepts. Tests are helllla hard too. Prof. Leditzky was a good lecturer, but I would personally take the online section.
He's a great professor and very considerate of students. I love his teaching style.

*NOTE RATING IS FOR MATH257: Prof. Leditzky has a thick accent and is difficult to understand at times, what was more problematic was his hard-to-read handwriting during lecture and poor explanation of topics. This class overall is a pain, tests are nothing like the homework with a heavy conceptual focus, and the coding is very irritating.

Incredible. 
Very direct and clear explanations and lectures. Very approachable outside of course as well.

analysis.name: Mitchell Fisher
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This was Mitch's first year as a UIUC professor, and I think he killed it. It is obvious he cares so much about his students. I think there are kinks in the format of the class to be worked out, but nonetheless, great professor. Mitch, if youre reading this, keep it up. Also, dont make the test worth 40% please.

Mitch is an awesome professor! He is new, so it took him a while to figure his stuff out but he is a very effective teacher that listens to feedback. He made ACCY 201 super informative and easy. Yes, the final is a lot of points and he is kind of a goofy guy, but he has given us really great opportunities to earn easy points.
Lots of not very good T.V./movie references. Also, for the first several weeks the class moves very slowly, continually repeating the exact same stuff.

Omg mitch fisher my king. so sweet. explains everything very well. plenty of resources to succeed. lots of extra credit. easy if u pay attention and follow along  in lecture and do the readings. so nice and a great prof, take with him if u can!
Does not seem very prepared when planning ahead. A lot of the grade is towards tests. Also, seems to try to hard to be funny, which has the opposite effect.

analysis.name: Frank Gallo
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very harsh grader compared to other professors. A lot of hidden requirements for speeches he wants to get a full score on certain categories. Too harsh for a communications beginner class.

This class was not hard at all. As long as you follow the rubric for each speech you're guaranteed an A. I am definitely not the best at public speaking but was still able to do really well. Truthfully, if you believe that he is a tough grader you are not following the criteria that he hands to you... also he is very nice!

He was the best professor I have ever had. He makes learning fun again. I had him last year, and I wish I could have him again! I see people from the class he taught all the time, and we never fail to bring up how badly we miss taking his class.

This professor TRIES to be funny, but harsh regarding grading. He's very very strict with format and is not tolerant. Took this non-native class, and he was strict with international students. Class is organized, but I feel like he's not the best at teaching, and we rarely did speaking activities compared to other classes. But gives a lot of info.

He tries to be funny and personable but his instruction and teaching technique is very poor. He doesn't really take correction or criticism well. Isn't considerate about mistakes or poor communication on his part and has a more "it is what it is" attitude when it causes a student to lose points rather than being lenient due to it being his fault.

analysis.name: Margaret Fleck
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 64 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Super friendly and a great lecturer. You can tell she really cares for her students. She goes out of her way to let students make up missed work and is always adjusting her course to teach it as effectively as possible. She wrote the entire textbook for the class and made it available to students online for free, which is greatly appreciated.

Examlets are worth a huge part of the grade, but they are pretty easy to study for with the given practice problems and past examlets. Lectures are a little helpful in solidifying material, but most of the learning comes from the textbook readings outside of class. She explains concepts in practical ways for students to understand.

Class isn't the best structured, but also not the worst. It focuses on BREADTH more than DEPTH. Quizzes are hard and test tiny details. MP's require self-learning Python.

Best advice: If you plan to take several AI-related courses (e.g. 446/447), then taking 440 first provides a good background and is useful; otherwise choose a different course.

Notes/videos/free textbook are great. Grade is fair but 90% tests with a few questions so easy to drop big on one mistake. Horrible lectures...seems to have forgotten her material? Spends 10 mins fighting the projector then the rest trying to remember how to solve the problem. Lots of mistakes/long pauses, says she's "demo-ing the process."

She is very knowledgeable and would periodically diverge from the lesson and discuss other applications of concepts. HW was very easy. However, you should check HW answers with a friend. To do well on tests, just make sure you study for understanding and not completion. The textbook, which she wrote, is very to-the-point and easy to understand.

analysis.name: Mitch Finch
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: It's a good class, just please please please make sure to dedicate a lot of time; it's definitely a big heavy lecture and workload class

I really enjoyed him as a person, he was super goofy. You get a point for every lecture you attend so it was worth it to go. Gave an extra credit assignment every week and the discussion homework was completion. The final was worth 40% and the midterm was 30% of the final grade so be sure to actually study or your grade will massively drop

analysis.name: Fataneh Taghaboni-Dutta
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: First I have to admit Professor Taghaboni-Dutta is very knowledgeable. My low rating is because she interrupts and talks over students who ask questions only to not fully answer the question. She also says homework should take 5 - 10 mins, yet several others said they took at least 3hrs on each assignment. Unrealistic expectations from her.

I have taken every graduate level class by Professor Taghaboni - she's an excellent teacher and provides real examples within her lectures to allow you to think through problems in an interesting way.  She encourages critical thinking skills and wants to teach you how to think about things not just do things. 
She doesn't put up with B.S.!

I'm so confused by the negative ratings here... Her classes were so great in my opinion and I've enjoyed learning from her.  She challenges you for sure but isn't that better than a boring class where its all minimum effort? Its graduate levels... 
She's been so great and is one of the best professors I've had in the program.
One of the best teachers at UIUC. Her stats class finally made me understand how statistics works, after having taken it on before in high school and college.
Never in my life have I had a professor where I do not understand anything she says. Truly, a marvel. She can speak for hours and no cohesive idea will be communicated.

analysis.name: Katherine Gaffney
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: She would literally post 13 assignments weekly. Like idk why she's posting assignments on a daily basis. I am in all advanced classes and none of them are this stressful than this level 1 class. I advise anyone to take RHET105 with a different professor please. This class makes me suicidal.

Not a professor but a  disorganized TA. Will harass you with emails especially over the weekend. Will lecture you if you didn't bring or print the paper after turning it in online. Most of our class didn't do some busy work she assigned and she flipped out. There is a lot to keep track of. I also paid for a book we hardly used.

Dr. G was great as an instructor. She did give a lot of homework, but a lot of it was the same from week to week. There are about 4 large writing assignments that you work on in, and go over in class. She is a tough grader but always gives a ton of feedback and is one of the most understanding professors that I have had.

Even though there is a lot of workload, the professor helps you a lot during office hours. She is a strict grader, but after you meet her during office hours and get her feedback, you will understand why you received that grade. If you need help with your grade, just go to her office hours.

ALWAYS willing to stay after, come in before, or schedule times to help students who actually care about improving their writing skills. Emails make it easy to know where you should be. A little preachy, but clearly knows what she is talking about. Super down to earth, easy to talk to, &Easily one of the best CW - Grad Students @UIUC!

analysis.name: Ghassan Moussawi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Took his class during this pandemic and he was awesome!! Super fun class, the chat was always active and the final project was not hard at all. I got to do a playlist for the final project, which I thought was super awesome and unique. The class topics were always very interesting and he always kept us engaged and nothing felt boring

Class was great. He's very passionate about what he teaches&helpful if you reach out individually. The only thing I didn't like was he'd get cranky if less than, like, 10 people volunteered to answer a question. I don't enjoy speaking in class due to social anxiety&I think the class environment could have been better equipped for that kind of thing

Professor Moussawi cares about his students and his field of study. He always asks provoking questions in class that lead to thoughtful discussion. There are powerpoints gone over in lecture, a quiz almost every week, and 2 papers-1regular1final.

Professor Moussawi is quite literally one of the best professors I have ever had. His class is the most enjoyable parts of my week! You can tell he truly cares about what he is teaching and his students! He is very engaging in lecture. Every time I leave his sections I am so inspired about the topic! If you can, definitely take his class!
Very engaging and energetic. You can tell he cares a lot about what he teaches! If you get the chance to take a class with him, 100% do it.

analysis.name: Toni Gist
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Toni is a great professor! Her lectures are very engaging and she does an amazing job breaking down the concepts so it's easier for students to understand. Toni is the best! She is so helpful both in and outside of class, and actually makes lecture interesting and go by fast. The workload for this class is light (about 30 min a week), and test questions come straight from her PowerPoint slides. Would totally recommend this class if you need a life science credit, or just an easy class to take.

This class is a great class to take for a science gen-ed. Toni sets you up to do well in the class and she makes sure everyone has the ability to get an A. If you do well on the assignments each week, go to class and actually listen and study for tests you're sure to do well and actually get something out of the class that will impact your health.

I absolutely loved professor Burkhalter's class. As a humanities major, I found FSHN 120 to be not only incredibly interesting but also very helpful. Professor Burkhalter gives interesting lectures and is beyond fair when it comes to grading. If you are looking to fulfill a gen-ed requirement with a great professor, take FSHN 120.

I loved Toni. I took FSHN 120 as a blowoff gen-ed, but she made me love nutrition and food sciences. She's an amazing lecturer and the content is actually very interesting. I hope she teaches more in-person classes, so that I can be her student again.

analysis.name: Mutha Gunasekera
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Reads off slides which he copies straight from the textbook. But then he puts in useless anecdotes and train-of-thought concepts that make no sense and makes the class nonsensical. His exams are twice as hard as any homework, quiz or online assignment. Bad teaching, worse prep. Also no retakes - not close to as good or lenient as other professors.

Terrible. Teaches a weed out class, but believes no one should be left behind, then has to increase the pace of the course to twice that of other classes in order to catch up. Puts material you havent learned yet on tests and expects you to answer E) Not enough information. Goes off on random tangents about how he is doing this for your benefit.

terrible. impossible to understand his trains of thought in lecture, and then half the exam has nothing to do with anything that was covered in lecture or from worksheets- and you're supposed to just know it, OR occasionally mark E on the scantron if it was something he expected you to not know!

Pretty cool guy but the material you end up being tested on is near impossible to fully study whether out of the book or past exams (which there are very few). He rarely curves and just taking notes from his lectures will not prepare you for the exams.

Dr.G is not a great teacher. His lectures were basically useless and they never helped me in discussion. I often felt like it was my first time seeing test question on the test. His quizzes are near impossible the first time around but he does do retakes. The only reason I'm going to pass the class is bc of all the EC. If you can take Hummel do it.

analysis.name: Molly Goldstein
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: She is a good professor and her class is graded on a lot (modelling exam, 4 sketching quizzes, 2 theory tests, weekly assignments, and 35% on the group project). You learn a ton in this class but the sketching quizzes and assignments are brutal and tiny mistakes will be there difference between 40/40 and a 15/40. The group project is a lot of work.

Prof Goldstein is honestly an amazing professor. Lectures can be a bit hard to follow so I recommend looking in the textbook/doing practice outside of class to get a better understanding. The group project is really important so make sure to communicate with your group members and don't procrastinate. Also make sure to study for the midterms.

SE101 was a lot of work and took a lot of effort, but Goldstein seemed to care more about how much effort you put in than final product. She is very understanding and great to talk to, as well as she gives great advice and direction. Her lectures are great and she provided more than enough resources to do well in the class.

Prof. Goldstein is the best ISE professor by far. This class was designed so well and I actually enjoyed and learned so much from it. Prof. Goldstein was accessible and understanding. I wish I could take this class again.

Professor Goldstein is a great person, but her lectures are useless. The TAs do the majority of the teaching - they do a great job. The class itself is very work heavy if you don't have a good group that prioritizes equal workload. The sketching and modeling homework is straightforward. The modeling exam and project determines your grade.

analysis.name: Mani Golparvar-Fard
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

Also, go to his office hours he is a great person to connect with if you want to continue in Construction Mgmt.

Mani loves teaching and is really passionate about the industry. He lays out goals before every class and will personally sit down with whoever does below average on a test to help them along.
Not the best professor, but very passionate about what he does. He wants all students to succeed.
Awesome professor, cares a lot about his students and wants them to suceed.

Great professor with great lectures that bring in outside experience and examples. Very useful content as well for future internships. TA's were not the most helpful but professor was always willing to chat outside of OH and help out.

analysis.name: Jeremy Guest
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Really passionate teacher which makes the hour and a half lecture not as painful. Willing to meet all the time, including coming in early and setting up extra study sessions. Constant group work though which can be a pain.

Best professor I've had in college. I actually changed my secondary field of study to Environmental Engineering after taking this class with Guest. Inspirational, makes the material easy to understand, and very reasonable with the gradings. Do not miss the chance to take a class with him!
Inspirational lectures and great guy. Learned a lot of real world skills in the class

One of my favorite professors I've had, just because he is very personable and his lectures are extremely clear. Environmental engineering isn't the most interesting topic, so lectures can be boring at times, but I have no doubt I would not have done as well as I did with a different teacher. Attendance is taken daily and all work is done in groups

Prof Guest is a very nice guy and he gives great lectures. I wasn't particularly interested in enviro, but I really enjoyed learning from him. You'll be working in the same group for weekly homeworks and a final project & presentation, and he has good policies in place to make sure your members pull their weight. Overall very enjoyable class!

analysis.name: Tibebu Haileleol
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lecture presentations definitely needs a bit more work. Expectations for certain parts of the assignments are clear but a good portion of other assignments were not clear. Needs balance. Needs to work with the TA more since our TA is sometimes unclear about Mr. Tibebu's instructions. Overall, his class structure is very poor but can be fixed

Professor does not follow what his syllabus says, based on his syllabus and what he said verbally in class, my Kahoot winning group was promised we will earn the 1.5 points from the Kahoot, but we only received 1 point. Our group emailed the professor, and he is unwilling to give us the extra 0.5 points since he needs to keep grading consistent.

Professor Tibebu is incredibly passionate about AI and AI accountability. You can clearly see his enthusiasm in every lecture, and he genuinely wants his students to become just as passionate. He always try we actually understand the material. Would take every class he offers.

An incredibly unorganized course. Lectures do not relate to weekly assignments. Discussion sections have repetitive 4-minute presentations every week from each group where notes of any kind & slides are banned. 

Every single assignment in this course is a group paper, so good luck getting your group on the same page & having everyone contribute.

I learned extensively about AI policy, regulation, national/international law. Some lectures were technical, including coding for responsible RAG and fairness metrics. Assignments drew from his research papers. He's helpful and accessible outside class, currently involving me in his research. He is strict on attendance.

analysis.name: Geoffrey Herman
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The class follows a flipped format, so there is not much interaction with the professor outside of office hours / other non-official meetings. However, he is clearly passionate about teaching and has put a lot of time and effort into developing the class materials to be as good as possible. A good class, interesting by virtue of its organization.

Herman is part of what makes CS@UIUC a top program. He structures the class so that you will learn through struggle. Though the content in the class may seem daunting, after each assignment you will appreciate how much you've learned. Grading is very generous, and it is clear in the way he manages his class that he wants every student to succeed.

One of the best CS courses I have took. Herman is just so nice and did really great job on how the course is structured. Even the content and quizs are pretty hard, but as long as you finished all the assignments, you are prepared. And they do provide you practice exam with multiple variants, so dont worry about that. And every quiz have a retake.

Prof. Geoffery Herman is a great professor! The course is hard but rewarding. While everything is on Prairielearn, there are very clear instructions and video explanations for harder questions. I attended the in-person section at 9 am, but I am motivated to go to CIF. The TAs and CAs are very helpful and caring.

The best course I've ever taken. It has a lot of work but it prepares you so well that you don't have to do anything extra for the quizzes/final exam. He gave a lot of extra credit and flexibility to make the class less stressful.

analysis.name: Steven Hall

Easiest class ever, pretty much just watched ads every class. Didn't learn too much, but Prof. Hall was funny and chill

analysis.name: Kellie Halloran

The quizzes are just like the homework, but the retry's get harder the later in the class you get so try to get a good score the first time.

I went to office hours for help on any HW problem I couldn't do, and that prepared me for the quizzes and final. TAM can be tough, but Halloran is great for it.

analysis.name: Yiju Huang

analysis.name: Jiajun He
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: So hes goated, i got an A- in the class and emailed him to bump it up and he did it with no questions asked to an A. You dont have to attend lecture but I'd recommend it because I think it personally helps you understand the content better. The homework is somewhat tedious but there's room for extra credit there.

This man is a robot, but a good one. His class runs at 8am, but you should go. Open-note quizzes and exams so take notes on paper. Very informative class on the basics of thermodynamics with 6 20-minute quizzes and 1 midterm. One drop for the quizzes. Final exam is heavily weighted and mainly covers later content such as cycles and psychrometrics.
He's genuinely a good professor.  Would go to lectures, they help.  Quizzes are easy and useful to study, midterm and final are chill.

analysis.name: Hongye Liu

I have taken two of his classes and wish he would just teach all of the CMN courses because he is that good!

BJ is awesome! He is one of those professors that you have in college that you'll never forget. He is both hilarious and helpful. He's very understanding whether you've made a mistake, turned in late work, and the like. Also, his classroom activities are fun and informative. Great guy, great class!

analysis.name: Jeanine Bensken
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very funny and interesting professor. She doesn't know much about some topics and won't be able to answer certain questions, but you can tell she cares and makes things interesting. Doesn't care much about helping you though. I broke a rib and asked for an extra day on an assignment and she refused. Easy class.
Boring class but fun teacher, very understanding of whatever happens. Very relaxed on due date timings.

Spring 2022. Was my GA. This was an advanced comp class, so it was more difficult. She is a tough grader but is willing to discuss your grade and change it if the examples were different. Would make room in her schedule to talk about course work and grades. Also, nice she will give letters of recommendation if you are a good student.

analysis.name: Elizabeth Luckman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Luckman is a very kind professor who is dedicated towards making her course as engaging as possible. She is a super caring person who personally checked in with me after hearing about personal issues that I had during the semester. Even though I personally didn't like Capsim, the way she structured her class made up for it. Best 201 prof.

Luckman is awesome! She facilitates an inclusive environment for all learners and really enjoys the subject. She grades fairly and makes all students feel welcome and encourages us to learn and grow. I could not have asked for a better experience. She is easy to access outside of class as well and empathizes with students.

Amazing professor. You can tell she actually cares about her students as people. The class is fun and interesting if you engage and make an effort to know your classmates. Would definitely recommend her for B201. And don't worry about the capsim simulation. It makes no sense at first, but you'll pick it up quickly.
Fantastic teacher and easy class! You can tell she really enjoys her subject.

She's a genuinely great professor, one of the better ones at UIUC. She doesn't just present material that we learn and forget just for a grade, she doesn't care about the grade rather she wants the student to grow as a person. She's all about participation and involvement in the material, so try to get interested in the class and ask questions.

analysis.name: Rakesh Bhatt
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Very good teacher. Humorous, interesting, and instructive. By attending his class i really feel like i did my work and got my rewards, and a well-deserved one. But he doesn't like people being late though

He talked a lot in his class and it was solely based on the readings. He often questions people who do not have their hand raised, so get ready to read. His TA was extremely nice and made it impossible for people to fail this class

First day in this class, I felt really interested. Professor Bhatt leads very good discussions; but tends to select a few students. This class was very easy. I got over 100% on everything.  Definitely a class I would recommend.
he has favorites and if you are not one of them, because you were not born a certain way he likes, good luck. avoid avoid avoid...

the worst professor i have ever met. he discriminates many students in the class. i also hope it is reported at some point. also, not a good teacher. lectures are boring and so hard to follow, zero structure.

analysis.name: Suma Bhat
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is the best out of the 120 professors this semester - explains concepts thoroughly and pauses for questions throughout the lecture. Overall, Bhat is a great professor and it's clear that she cares about her students unlike the other professors.
great professor, learned a lot in her classes and helped with the exams and homeworks in the class

Ok at best, her lectures are hit and miss on whether or not they make sense. If it's a really technical topic, watch Jaramillo's lecture videos, because he's way better at explaining things. The test in this class are pretty tough too, especially since the TA's grade them so ruthlessly. If you can I would get someone else for ECE 120 lecture.

Suma was OK at teaching the relatively simple concepts, but for the more difficult ones, I would come out of lecture not understanding anything. For a lot of it, I had to go back and watch lecture videos from the other professors, and a lot of the time there was no time to do that so I just had to figure it out from friends or from YouTube.
Great lecturer. She articulates the class materials very well and she cares about the learning experience of students. Very good lecturer in general.

analysis.name: Rohit Bhargava
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lots of work and hard grading is the story of this class.  Basically is the course work of 3 seperate classes all put together into 1.  Bhargava sees undergrads the same as grad students and has the same expectations.  Kinda ridiculous but probably going to be a useful class in the long run

The exams were tough and the homework was crazy. But the final grade was better than I expected. Really helpful guy but I was very scared to go up to him. Starts asking questions back if you ask him any.
This class is tough! Too much work but Bhargava is helpful if you speak to him. Kind of a cool guy in a weird way. Speak to him and find out that he really cares that the students learn.
makes you go to class and calls you out if you even yawn. But he is brilliant and funny. Really knows his stuff.
ha ha poor sophomores been asking me how his class is :-)

analysis.name: Mardia Bishop
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The class overall is great but she gossips.

I had her for CMN496. The class was pretty pointless. With only 9 people in class we basically listened to her conversations with the TA. This class is nothing like it sounds, but if you need an easy elective I would do it. 5 short questions on plays and 2 exams.

Mardia is a great teacher for CMN101. She can be weird and quirky at times, but it's why students love her. You are required to buy the workbook for this class and you will definitely use it. My tips: Do every assignment (grade boosters!), get to class early on days you might sign up for speech times, sit in the front of the room, and PARTICIPATE!!
Dr. Bishop genuinely cares about her students and wants them to improve their public speaking skills, so she gives a lot of feedback and is always willing to help out before or after class.

Awesome all around teacher. Really willing to help students and take time out of class to go over tough material or issues with grades. Speeches are medium difficulty, and definitely need work put in out of class. Go to lecture and do your work, and you've pretty much got an A

analysis.name: Elizabeth Bigsby
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Not the worst but her monotone voice and attitude towards students made me rate her a bit lower. At times I couldn't tell if she was purposely being a little rude or if her energy is just a little bit cold. The visual analysis would be annoying because it would be in groups and her grading was specific. Only good thing were online Friday classes.

prof. bigsby is a great professor who seems to enjoy what she does/teaches! Her class is interesting and easy as long as you show up to lecture and pay attention. There are weekly quizzes but you can drop a couple and then exams and one final group project that is fun! Her class is really enjoyable and fun to learn about!

Professor Bigsby is so awesome. Study before the tests, come to the lecture, and you'll get a high A for sure! I really love this class and she clearly cares and knows the material very well. Also-- participate! It's not necessarily mandatory but it definitely shows her you know what you're doing. Nothing but good things to say.

Dr. Bigsby is an amazing professor. She really knows her stuff and keeps her lectures interesting. This course is nothing like CMN 321(which was awful). It's very interesting content and she breaks up the lectures with class activities. Fair grader and the book is easy to read. Daily writing summaries, 3 exams, 1 paper, and 1 final research paper.

She gives quizzes on each reading you do for class. You are not aloud to use the notes you may have taken so you essientially have to study each reading before each quiz. Also the lectures are not helpful and pretty much had to teach myself everything because she gave little to no clarification. No notes or structure given.

analysis.name: Cabral Bigman-Galimore
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: There are a lot of assignments in this class, and most of them are group work. However, the assignments aren't too hard and Prof Bigman was always available to help. She provided study guides that helped me get good exam scores. There were also in-class quizzes that usually I didn't do well on and there's a presentation at the end of the semester.

Exam was killer, class median was 65 with average of 69 with no intention to curve or do test corrections. Project has been a wild ordeal, little guidance and unorganized check points. I cannot get an A anymore due to the exam so im pretty much coasting the rest of the year for any B. Id stay away and take a much easier class.

Be upfront about her needing to lecture slower (doesn't post her slides but has PARAGRAPHS of info on them), the final paper has some nonsensical source requirements + she isn't clear on what you are doing exactly content wise, and expect this class to take up a lot of time from the reading (that has related assignments due before each class).

The amount of homework to pass this class is absurd. The material is very interesting but the professor is obsessed about homework for every single class. Moreover, you have 3 exams (about 45 multiple questions + 5 essay questions) and a final essay. If you're taking other courses be aware that this course will take a lot of your time.

Prof Bigman is a very kind person and very knowledgeable, but her lectures are so boring and some the material taught makes no sense. Exams are tough but assignments are easy. She can be a tough grader. I've gotten a lot of 9.2/10. Lots of material to know for midterms. I've had her for 2 different courses and I dread going to both. She is kind tho

analysis.name: Billie Spencer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great pedagogue; able to explain complex, difficult, concepts and problems that will make your head spin. Excellent teacher and a leader in his field. However, the workload is obscene. Also, he missed about 8 lectures, including his own final and three lectures prior to the midterm. Takes lots or trips to China; nobody holds him accountable...

Poor explaining during his lectures and instead quickly goes through example problems without explanation of where anything comes from. He was only at  ~50% of the lectures throughout the semester with zero accountability. Yet when a student is gone for research/conference, he is not accommodating as he denies requests for the lecture recordings.
It is a very dedicated professor but it is not clear. The subject its really demanding but not conceptually clear. I found it not good in the end. To much work and not much learned.

He is not a good lecturer.  He diverted attention from the main principles of the class by getting us to focus on MATLAB, which was unnecessary for the subject material.    The book he asked us to purchase was terrible. There are books of better quality on the market that he could have recommended.  He showed very little interest in our learning.

Good professor, very smart. However, if you go ask him a question and you are not an Asian female, he will be very condescending. Do not go to his office hours, you will be ignored. The class overall is run well. Tests aren't impossible and the homework is from the book and relatively easy, but this class TAKES A LOT OF TIME

analysis.name: Billy Vermillion
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Billy is awesome. Period. He explains things so clearly. His method of teaching is conducive to learning- watch a movie, discuss readings about the movie and other topics, watch clips that tie both readings and movie together. These clips provide inspiration for papers. I've said too much. Billy is awesome, if you have a chance, take his class.

This guy really likes what he's doing, and that makes class so much more fun. He's seen every movie and explains things really well. Three 5-6 page papers and a midterm in class, no final (we had a final paper instead). Just come to class, do the papers, and enjoy. This guy is fun. I'd take him again.

Great teacher, but would recommend that you take a general film course before this, because he expects you to have a basic knowledge of film techniques and skills before entering the class. Always open to questions. Would recommend.
Professor Vermillion is so fun, caring and a great lecturer!

analysis.name: Jessica Birkenholtz
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class was supposed to be an easy A before she replaced the previous teacher. She tries too hard to be cultural, and poorly reads off powerpoints. Exams were a lot of writing. Study hard, and an A is doable.

She is a good professor, but the course itself is much more advanced for a 100-level class. Weekly quizzes are not too bad if you go to lecture, but she only has one midterm and four essays before the final, and the midterm was pretty hard. Make sure to read the assigned texts and try to stay on top of what she says in lecture.

Boring lectures. Reads off slides. Make sure you understand the material by closely reading the books. Do not depend on the lectures and TA sections. Weekly quizzes, and they are not the easiest. Tests are difficult, long, and require a lot of analysis; no practice exams. On a scale of 1-10, the amount of effort you have to put in for an A is 8.

This Introduction to Hinduism class seemed far from an introductory course. She expected us to all have a pretty solid foundation of knowledge in the religion. Many of the students in my class did have a solid foundation and she seemed to enjoy them more. Would not take again. Hard A and tests incredibly lengthy and detailed. GL

Knows what shes talking about but spends so much time talking there wasnt a single day she didnt go a few minutes past when class was supposed to end.  Theres a ton of reading and no time to catch up. If you end up taking the class (which I honestly dont recommend) watch out for the final paper because she gives you zero time time to work in class

analysis.name: Blake Johnson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: You will learn the ways of Blake Johnson. He is a legend. The class can be difficult, but Blake is always there to cheer everyone up, sort of, kind of.  Great professor, even better guy.

I have mixed opinions about this class. Very time consuming, especially at the beginning and during admin terms w all the meetings. Johnson is a somewhat strict professor overall. At the same time I feel like this class has taught me a lot of useful engineering skills. And the grading is complicated but they're pretty lenient on larger assignments.

Johnson wasn't bad on his own. However, the course grading was unfair, and ultimately the quizzes single-handedly destroyed my otherwise perfect grade. Despite doing well on the final, homework, and showing up to every classes, the quizzes tore my grade apart. Unsure if these are his fault or not, but as the professor, it needs to be partly on him.

Blake Johnson is why ME 310 and 320 are so inconsistent in their labs. The TAs are not well-briefed on their labs or how to grade the labs, leading to very unclear in-class activities and even more inconsistent grading. In reviewing other section's work, I found that I received significantly lower grades for better work. He needs to step it up!

The class is a lot of work, especially depending on your group members. Generally, it's a free A although grading can be tough on certain assignments. Blake can be disrespectful/rude to students especially during presentations. However, you will learn a lot in 470

analysis.name: Dan Block
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dan is a great guy but beware that his classes are heavy on work. the grading isn't hard and its relatively easy to get an A if you put in the work for it, but that usually means lots of hours outside of class/labs per week. He expects you to come into the lab to work on all of your homework so you can't just do it at home on your schedule.

Dan is really hands-on guy. ME461 taught by him is a good course if you want to gain more experience on the hardware side and see how exactly things like micro-controllers work. The lectures are decent but it is mostly from the labs, that you learn the most. His grading is pretty reasonable and course load is not that much

Dan is hands down the best professor I had at UIUC.  I've learned more useful information from him than every other class, and his classes are the reason I got my job so easily.  Truly cares about his students, and will do anything to help.  His classes are very easy to get an A in if you do the work, which isn't always easy.  Highly recommend him

If you take any controls labs at the U of I, you will no doubt work with Dr. Block. One of the best professors and classes I have taken in undergrad. Dr. Block is very reasonable and works harder on his courses than any other professor/lecturer I've ever taken a class with. He wants you to learn and enjoy learning and I appreciate that.

Block is admired for developing the class so I was excited. But, he mocked mistakes, loudly. Lectures were unorganized and labs were four full hours a week. It was hard to focus with him hovering and nitpicking. I want a class where trying something new and failing, is okay. He also leans on our shoulders when he's frustrated.

analysis.name: Ken Blank
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Blank was a great professor, very understanding and kind! He wouldn't try to trick us on assignments or exams, and would prioritize our learning and our comprehension. He was also fair in general, and would give back points often. The MCB department made a terrible mistake when removing Blank from his position and I think they should be ashamed

I didn't know he was fired, thought he just quit due to backlash from students. Most beneficial MCB department moment, I love them so much! They are so cool and I never knew that I could meet people that are so nice!

I was sad to find out that they fired him. He was a nice guy who wasn't given the resources he needed by the MCB department. Totally believe he would've done well with teaching what we needed to know if they gave him some more direction instead of just throwing him into it.
We need him back in MCB, was my favorite professor and they got rid of him after a few weeks, terrible decision.
He was a great professor but wasn't given a chance by the department

analysis.name: Steven Blanke
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is very generous and super approachable. Very fair by spreading the exam questions evenly for every lecture. After every lecture, he goes back to the slides and adds extra necessary info which was super helpful. His exam questions were sometimes vague, but overall exams were fair and reflected the material covered in class only (not readings).

Prof Blanke is very very knowledgeable and knows the material very well. He does a good job bridging topics and making important connections and answers questions well. I'm not too fond of the huge amount of points figure presentations are worth, especially if you happen to end up with a lame figure. Study hard and attend class, and you'll do fine!

One of the GOATS here at UIUC. Class structure is great; pre recorded lectures with in person discussion and online discussion board (Packback). He did an amazing job of covering many intro microbiology topics while still giving us interesting details, including things pre-meds, pre-dents, pre-pharm students will find particularly interesting

He's an okay teacher. His lecture slides are LOADED with stuff, yet you only get tested on a fraction of it, so its hard to know what youre supposed to study. Had him for the second half of MCB 300 (first half was taught by Cari vanderpool) and his teaching/testing style literally ruined my perfect grade of an A+.

analysis.name: AnnaMarie Bliss
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class was pretty easy. Because of COVID everything was online/zoom: lecture once a week and studio once a week. She offered a lot of extra credit opportunities. We had do to a weekly discussion post, quiz and weekly reading, not hard. There was a lot of drafting involved was time consuming, but not too difficult.

Dr. Bliss clearly cares about her students. She does so much out of class to make sure her students feel supported which meant a lot to me as a freshman with all online classes. She knows a lot and is amazing at sharing her knowledge. Her assignments are well thought out and manageable. I felt like I learned a lot.
An amazing mentor and guide throughout the 2 courses. She is like a friend who is accessible and I can reach out to her for any of my personal struggles. Will 100% recommend her.
Very understanding and easy to access and teach

analysis.name: Nancy Blake
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I think the others explain her perfectly! Her class wasn't too bad except she was very vague about the exam content. She flat out said to just study EVERYTHING for the exams with no study guide or anything, although paying attention to recurring themes in lecture hint at the exam contents. I didn't like that she was so vague in that way.

I wasn't too impressed by the class. Lectures were bare bones slides she threw together right before coming to class, and the four response papers we had to write I basically wrote in 10 minutes and my only feedback was a letter grade and a one-word descriptor - "great", "good", "excellent", etc. I didn't learn much but I got to see cool films

Prof. Blake was an absolute joy to have as a professor. The class was on the second half of French and Comparative Cinema, and the list of films was incredibly curated. I enjoyed almost every film screened in class, and the PPT presentation she gave following the film gave new insight. The assignments were manageable and interesting. Great Prof!

Nancy Blake is the worst professor at the University of Illinois. She studied under eminent theorist Jacques Lacan and obviously learned nothing. She quoted wikipedia and Sparknotes gratuitously and spoke in a slow, inoculating tone. She is awful and hope that you never have to take a class with her. Grading is completely based on your TA.

I loved this class. Professor Blake's discussions were provocative and I had an amazing experience with her. She is vague about grading and projects, but I found her enjoyable. Her style of teaching isn't for everyone, but if you have any interest in the subject matter, her classes are great.

analysis.name: Joel Blanco
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Horrible Teaching Assistant. One of the worst classes I've taken at U of I.

He's a great teacher, and has a pretty good sense of humor. You don't have to show up to class, but he does do pop quizzes. If you don't do the small readings and study the pp you won't do well. His tests are completely based on his pp, word for word. Easy A.
Joel is really laid back. Attendance is mandatory because there are pop quizzes and in-class writings. It was pretty easy.
He was difficult and gave me lots of unecessary stress
Easy A. Teacher personality very poor.

analysis.name: Jochen Bojanowski
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He taught pretty well and his lecture videos were very helpful in understanding the readings. It was honestly just a lot of work, from video lecture notes, to live lecture assignments, weekly annotations, video assignments, and exams. The main thing I didn't like was having to annotate a long article every week, but class was thought provoking.

Entertaining and easy if you're willing to put in the effort. It's an ACP class, so expect essays for an exam, but note that the essay is easy as long as you know your material. For example, what are the views of the philosophers in question and have an example or two prepared. ProctorU is terrible, but it can't be helped bc of ChatGPT cheaters.

This class is very doable. 2 readings (annotations) every week which takes about 2 hours. The 8AM essays exams were annoying but the TAs grade pretty fair and the regrade was generous. I averaged an 80 on the first ones and 88 after regrade. There's 7 pts extra credit too. The class is disorganized though so you need to stay on top of it.

This class is awful. He says he gives you a optional zoom. THAT SHIT IS NOT OPTIONAL. You have to go. Also the way everything is structured sucks. This is a gen ed but he treats it like its the entrance to the military.

Good lectures and the exams were easy enough as long as you read the texts/ watched the lectures. Heads up for a bunch of Canvas notifications but they are mainly small daily assignments. Tons of extra credit and regrade opportunities so nothing to complain about here

analysis.name: Marni Boppart
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class is one of the best courses in the KIN department. It gives you a basic understanding of exercise physiology, and Dr. Boppart is an excellent lecturer. Put in the hard work and you will succeed in this class. The labs are fun too! If you don't enjoy this class, then you're not a true Kinesiology student.

Prof. Boppart clearly knows what she's talking about. Some people might think of her as hard to approach or scary, but once you talk to her you realize this is not the case. This is probably the hardest 100 level KIN class, but it's very interesting. There isn't much work outside of class, but you have to have to understand the lectures well

Prof. Boppart was (in my opinion) a good lecturer. She could be monotone at times, but make sure you take notes in class. Few assignments are graded, aside from a weekly quiz. If you pay attention, these quizzes are not hard, and she also drops your two lowest quiz grades. She also offers study sessions outside of class time for the unit exams.

Great lecturer, very knowledgeable. Only downside is little to no extra credit, and quizzes can make or break your grade (missing a question drops your grade to a 75%). Great at explaining difficult concepts but tends to be quite monotone in lectures. Offers review sessions and appointments to discuss grades if/when struggling.

Random quizzes worth 10 points about 15 over the semester.  Lab homework isn't pretty easy, lab only meets every other week. Do good on labs and set for at least a B. Tests aren't all that bad, get easier as semester goes on. Overall good teacher and depending on your TA can be really good.  Gives study guide for all tests as well as review session

analysis.name: Eric Bolton
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Bolton's lecture style is pretty dry and he goes over certain concepts  multiple times, but the material is really interesting and lectures were always clearly organizedeasy to understand.  Exams are fair and he's not out to trick you.  He's a good guy and is approachable after class or in office hours.
He is a really good lecturer and sets up a clear criteria for grading-an extremely fair class where the grade you get is equivalent to the effort you put into the class.

Professor Bolton was fine for the half of the class that was in person, but once we switched to online learning during the pandemic, he basically just stopped teaching all together. He sent us his notes on the powerpoint slides and basically told us to teach ourselves.

The most boring lecturer ever. Seriously. Exam questions come from the slides, the class material is interesting and easy to self-teach. You just need to make a Quizlet of concepts and straight up memorize all of it. Easy A class overall.
He's a pretty nice guy. Engages the class well. He only teaches a small portion of endocrinology, three class periods, and he did a decent job teaching.

analysis.name: Simeon Bogdanov
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Best professor I had in UIUC. Took his ECE340 and now taking ECE405 with him. His lectures are so easy to understand and explains everything well. Very willing to answer questions and explains everything well.

One of the best professors I have had in UIUC. His analogies are very helpful for explaining hard concepts. He is always enthusiastic and prepared of lectures and is very accessible in office hours and after class. Strongly encourages taking his interactive lectures and participate in his questions.
Very good professor, made a very tough course (some may argue the toughest in EE curriculum) feel like a breeze. Engaging lecture, good presentations, would recommend

Absolutely fantastic professor. His lectures are engaging and he presents such descriptive analogies for the complex topics covered in ECE 340. He truly cares that students come to conclusions themselves instead of just giving the explanation. Would highly recommend his teaching style for those who like to learn through the lecture.

analysis.name: Ben Clegg
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 177 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Clegg is a very nice man, but an incredibly ineffective professor. His lectures are often incoherent, ambiguous and convoluted. He very frequently takes simple concepts and makes them very difficult to understand. The TAs in this class know almost nothing about the topic, and are incredibly difficult to work with.

Clegg is a funny man, very energetic and obviously passionate about biology. His test are nothing like his slides, notes, etc. They are mostly critical thinking problems which makes them extremely difficult and confusing. Some would say this is a blow off class, I beg to differ.

Clegg literally jumps at the chance to help his students. He is a good teacher because of his great passion for biology and he really cares about his students whether he knows their names or not. He is a really good guy. On the negative side, he can occasionally ramble and his lectures can be a tad confusing.

I really disliked this class. Basically edged us with clicker pts at the end of lecture (ppl would leave) bc he went overtime almost every class. Discussion wasn't helpful. Never used textbook, and the homework was tedious, though the practice tests were somewhat helpful. People glazing but I hated it. I failed every exam, BUT ended with a C sooo.

He talks a lot and honestly it interferes with learning the material since he is constantly talking away.. he will try to make a point yet go in a thousand different directions and never truly reach a conclusion. analysis.name: Valeria Bonatti
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

She was a great professor, honestly. Very willing to help and encouraging. However, she was not always up to date on her grades. You won't pass without the textbook. She is a repeat offender of posting assignments without telling the students. Quiz, data collecting and 45-50 page chapter reviews every single week. The lectures were full of concepts that were hard to pay attention to and understand. Multiple lengthy readings per week. Prof is very caring, but intense concepts for 100 lvl class.

There was quite a bit of reading, and it helped if you did it, but she basically went over the reading in class. Also, she posted all of the reading on Moodle for us, so you don't have to buy a book necessarily.
