Super sweet and friendly, good lecturer. Being online, I struggled to pay attention in class bc they were very long and slow paced, but overall good at explaining. However, shes really tough on grading the Computational HW. The exams were pretty hard, and she will not provide answers to the study guides. Youll need to study a lot!
Prof Leal is one of the best I've had at UI. Her lectures are great and she cares a lot about her students. Textbooks are used but UI students have free access to all of them. Highly recommended.
Dr. Leal is an absolute queen. Her class is very interesting, and I feel like I am learning a lot without being overwhelmed in work.

analysis.name: Cedric Langbort
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I don't understand why anybody would spend their life thinking about how a communication channel sends information strategically. The only reason seems that it pays for his tenured job. But his research makes no sense & why a PhD student would spend 5 years thinking about this stuff and then go to industry unless you are from a developing nation

This was probably the worst class that I have taken. Professor Langbort has consistently been one of the worst professors and yet is still teaching. It is a shame that students are paying to suffer through this poorly designed and taught course. The only positive is that the graders are typically generous and have saved my grade countless times.
Very hard exams, and long homework assignments. Course notes are handwritten, not organized well, and hard to read.
Great professor. although his courses are a bit math heavy. so comfort with reading math should be good

Professor Langbort's teaching is great, but can be confusing. Lecture notes are at a fundamental, but assigned homework (5-6, drop 2) are absolutely brutal. For one homework, I went to 2 office hours to solve 1 problem (out of 3). If you want a challenging but rewarding class, this course might be for you. You will learn a lot, or nothing at all.

analysis.name: Francesco Cellarosi
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I had the pleasure of having Dr. Cellarosi as my professor for MATH 241 last semester. I have never had a professor as passionate, energetic, and engaging as Dr. Cellarosi. Vector calculus is a difficult class and he made every attempt to explain the underlying conceptual basis of the material. Highly recommended.

Cellarosi is amazing.  There are many concepts that were pretty difficult for me to grasp, but he made it entertaining and possible!  The tests were very hard, but the curve worked out for everyone in the end.  Also, willing to meet with students one-on-one.

Gives very clear explanations and is very passionate about math.  Also tells a fair share of funny jokes.  I consider myself a good math student and had only gotten A's before this class.  Even if you are fully prepared, there is usually 1-2 tricky question on each exam.  By far the best professor for this course (average scores higher than others)
Fantastic professor. He's very energetic and excited during his lectures. Sometimes, I just show up so I can listen to his Italian accent. Very approachable person.

I had Cellarosi at UIUC for Calc 3. He was absolutely amazing. His lectures always maintained higher averages than the other professors, and he was clear and concise during class. He always added a touch of comedy (but not trying too hard) during lecture to keep students' attention. Besides, he's always wearing something artistically extravagant.

analysis.name: Cele Otnes
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is really nice and her tests are very straight forward and not meant to trick you. I took the class last semester, there were pop quizes in class so attendance is mandatory. The online homework is very easy. If you skim through the book you'll get an A, if you don't then if you have a good amount of common sense you could probably pull off a B

Her knowledge on the subject is shallow, and her lectures are dry. Seems she did not have much to teach you except summarizing the outlines. She encourages students to tell very personal stories about their lives, to spend a big portion of the class time on. The more talkative you are about your dramatic private life, the more she likes you.

Though the examples she use is interesting, the way she lectures just makes me fall asleep in class. Her tests are easy if you've read the book, though you can answer most of the questions with common sense. The grading for the article analysis is tough though. She makes us spend money to buy an account to do useless homework assignments.

Well, her exams are not bad. You just have to study the slides and write down things she reiterate in class. I don't think she does a good job of making powerpoint slides...it is very disorganized. She only quiz you on stuff she thinks is important. Textbook is a rip off, you need it for homework and 1/5th of your studying.

Otnes is engaging and interesting in what could otherwise be a dry and boring class; examples and lectures are very relevant. Exams are easy, just review her slides and articles (and there are no more pop quizzes). Homework, however, is useless and not even included on exams, but you have to do it...Overall, a nice easy A.

analysis.name: Max Christie
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He's one of the nicest professors I've ever had. The lab can be a bit challenging if you've never done geography before. For exams, definitely go to class and focus on the study guide. The slides are posted, but they mostly have pictures, so they can be confusing if you didn't attend lecture.

Guy is one of the best lecturers at Illinois, seriously go to his class if you take it. Lab section was annoying in my opinion but course is really dope. He's a passionate and great dude. Tests are pretty light and final exam is low stress due to his grading system. Completely free textbooks-wise. Definitely recommend

Prof. Christie is an very entertaining and passionate lecturer. Attendance is optional but there's no point in taking this class if you don't attend his lectures. The weekly Packbacks and labs are free and the homework readings are short and less frequent. Quizzes and exams are also very easy. Goated professor.

An excellent lecturer, just a joy to listen to in class and he makes the material so interesting. Grading is good, homework is light and discussions are always interesting. Some memorization will be required but with the subject taught so well, this doesn't ever feel like a burden. I loved this class and Christie is the best lecturer I've had.

Best lecturer I've ever had. Makes class interesting, fun, and easily understandable. Extremely open to questions during class and willing to clarify all confusing points. Will give hints about what is on the test during the lecture. YOU WANT TO BE AT LECTURE. It makes the class so much easier. FREE TEXTBOOK and you only pay for Packback.

analysis.name: Ciro Incoronato
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Ciro truly cares about the subject matter he teaches as well as the well-being of his students. His experience as an Italian American academic makes his lectures and interactions with his students even more profound. He even took us out to lunch for one of his classes. Stand up guy!

Ciro is a great professor and clearly knowledgeable about his field not only because he did his research, but because he's actually from Italy and has experienced some of the things we've talked about in class, and certainly has learned much about the history of Rome in his time growing up there. The content was interesting and engaging!
Ciro is the best professor at UIUC. His lectures are engaging and you can tell he knows what he is talking about. His grading is fair and I would definitely take another course with him.

analysis.name: Valerie Cintron
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: 400 not 402. Gives vague directions on assignments and then is nitpicky while grading. Valerie is deaf but lectures completely verbally and sometimes it can be difficult to understand what she is saying. For online lecture she just talked without stopping then sent us to do group work. My breakout groups didn't really know what she wanted from us.

Professor Cintron is a great professor but it can be a little difficult to understand her which could be a problem for some. But, she was always willing to fix any barriers and was very informative about the topics. There are quizzes every Sunday and a few projects and assignments but most of them are writing assignments. There is a group project.

I don't know if it's Covid or what, but this semester has been a disaster. She doesn't return emails or check in with students for WEEKS. The quizzes are filled with mistakes that she refuses to fix and sent a defensive email when she received feedback about it. Classes are poorly organized. I got more out of my interactions with peers than her.

There are assignments due for each class, they usually are pretty short though. Sometimes her grading criteria is unclear but she is willing to work with the students to change. There is A LOT of small group work so be prepared to meet EVERYONE in your class because she will make you work with different people multiple times in one class period.

Valerie is a very tough grader, don't expect much slack when justifying a diagnosis in your assessments. I had a hard time with the 1st big essay & midterm and was panicking. Valerie met with me twice and clearly broke down the work & her expectations, with her guidance I sailed through the rest of the assignments. Exceptionally good professor.

analysis.name: Julie Cidell
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Cidell is kind and always willing to answer questions. Thought class would be more interesting (Cities of the World) but is just ok. More of an urban planning course. Exams aren't bad (combo of readings & lecture) and three easy projects throughout the semester. Readings assigned for homework (5-15 pgs) which is not included in lectures.

I have taken 2 courses with Dr. Cidell and she is the single most impactful professor that I've had in my four years at UIUC. Dr. Cidell is knowledgeable, caring, and creates an environment conducive to student success. It is a pleasure to listen to her lectures and take part in conversations in her courses. I couldn't recommend GGIS 465 enough.

Julie is amazing out of class during her office hours and her lectures are very engaging and streamlined. Tests are fair but make sure you do the required readings as parts of the exam draw directly from reading material not touched on in lecture. There are also frequent mini papers and two larger assignments but those were pretty manageable.

Engaging lectures and super nice lady! There's a lot of reading but if you follow the reading schedule on the syllabus and dont fall behind you'll be ok! Midterms are not too bad, she gave very thorough study guides beforehand. Good professor and the class is very doable.

She drops a decent amount of assignments but there are two weekly assessments (a lab and a quiz) so it's a decent amount to keep track of if you're in other demanding classes. The textbook is used for at least half of the quizzes. However, she's super nice and a great lecturer. Great to talk to outside of class if you're struggling and in general.

analysis.name: Josue Cisneros
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I don't have enough words to type how caring Professor Cisneros is, and he's VERY passionate about what he teaches. True to the material (social movements), he doesn't agree w/ graded assignments, we're told to give ourselves (fair) grades. There aren't papers or tests, decent amount of daily reading/discussion though. Participation is important!!

Professor Cisneros is a great teacher to take. I took 396 Intercultural Rhetoric and it was extremely well organized and expectations were clearly stated from the start. You MUST participate every class period and read read read! I would not recommend if you aren't going to read the materials. Great professor and very well organized.

The class was very easy. No tests or papers, and the occasional homework here and there. The class is flipped so the class meetings are more of a discussion and you grade yourself at the end of the course. He is a very sweet instructor and cares about what he teaches!
He's very knowledgeable about what he teaches, he just isn't engaging. It's a struggle to pay attention in his class, he's very low energy. But it's an easy A so it's whatever.

I absolutely loved the class I took with Cicneros, The Rhetoric of Social Movements, it was interesting and he seemed genuinely interested in the material he was teaching. He was a fair grader and if you participate in class he will give you a good grade.

analysis.name: Amanda Ciafone
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are mandatory since she doesn't post notes online and there are iclicker points. 2 lectures and 1 discussion. 2 papers in discussion that are pretty easy. 3 exams and no final. Good amount of extra credit. 1 group project where you make a short film. You have some readings on compass, but can do without. Overall fun class!

Easy and interesting class. I didn't study for one exam and am going to get an A or A+. Literally do the readings(I did them but you probably don't even have to do those), watch the movies, and pay attention in lecture (which shouldn't be hard because she is a great lecturer) you'll get an A no problem. A really fun class that covers 2 GenEd Reqs.

You don't need to buy a textbook which is nice. There is only readings and projects as homework. The reading is manageable and only skimming will work. I didn't read after the first 4 and I was fine. There are no tests and the final is a 7 page essay. She is nice, smart and makes everyone feel welcome. Class can be boring but content is cool.
so interesting to listen to in lecture. knows her stuff since she has worked in the industry. love love love.

Very left leaning, which isn't surprising. Other than that, the class was very easy. There are a lot of readings but you can easily get by without them. The tests claim to be based off of them, but most of the info on the tests is straight from lecture. Just go to lecture and you'll be fine. Final project was a lot of time but fun.

analysis.name: Andrei Cimpian
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: BEST. CLASS. EVER. Prof. Cimpain is great. The class is extremely interesting, and grading is fair. If you study hard, you should have no problem acing it. He is always willing to help if you have a question. But be warned- the class involves a lot of reading (especially of journal articles), so if that is a problem for you, I would not take 462.

Very good professor! He makes an intro class quite intriguing with a lot of examples. He's very knowledgable and always willing to answer questions during the class. Exams are very straightforward, just follow the review sheet and you'll do great. Best choice.

Very straightforward, attendance was not required but extra credit opportunities were offered in class which removed stress for the exams! Just study everything discussed in lecture and the tests will go fine.

Andrei is very nice and helpful when you reach out to him. However, he is not the most exciting lecturer. This is a pretty standard intro class, and not difficult at all if you take notes during the lectures.

Dr. Cimpian is the best. His lectures are so clear and you can tell he has an in-depth understanding of the literature. He definitely made me more interested in learning about child and cognitive development.

analysis.name: Cinda Heeren
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 77 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Cinda is one of the best professors I've had. She's super chill and easy to talk to. Going to her class isn't necessary (lectures are online), but I benefitted a ton by going to lectures and asking questions. She understands your questions and gives great explanations. I have never written a review for a professor before but Cinda is worth it! :)

Amazing woman! Tests are tough, but she loves what she does and is so passionate. Very approachable, and is very willing to answer questions. She knows her stuff and cares about her students. MPs are hard, but we're CS @ Illinois. You will learn a lot from Cinda and from going to lecture! Highly recommend her! One of my favorite teachers ever. :)

Cinda is a great lecturer who is very enthusiastic and covers material well. The TAs & piazza will be your main source of help with questions on material/mps/labs. Though the MPs and material may be difficult, it is worth it. Plus, there's extra credit. Lectures are also online but on occasion slides can be glitchy. Work hard and it'll pay off.

Professor Cinda Heeren is the best professor I ever had. She is caring about students to learn the material properly and enjoy the class. She keeps involving students in the class. I took CS121 at UBC with her and she is great in relating the material to upper year courses (CS221).

Cinda is amazing. Data Structures, with her at the helm, has been the best class I've had at UIUC. It's one of the few that has really made me feel like I'm actually in a world class program. She will challenge you but also give you all the tools you need to succeed.

analysis.name: Dionne Clifton
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I really liked Dionne's class! I thought it was a fun class to scatter through my tougher classes! I'm not sure why she doesn't have a higher rating tbh. You can tell she deeply cares about the world of sales. She's highly knowledgeable in this field, as she has a real estate brokerage, which I feel only adds to the course! Just do the HW and EC!

Dionne is a nice person who has done well for herself in the world of sales and real estate, but her class sucks. She makes students buy a separate platform for discussion posts instead of using Canvas or other free platforms. She made us purchase pdfs that were mostly available for free online. Her class was an easy A, but not an enjoyable one.

Many reviews on here have a negative rating of the ADV320 ONL course and Dionne, which I don't understand. Personally, I don't feel strongly on her, but I didn't mind the class. This course is very easy as its dependent on Canvas Quizzes, short papers, and discussion posts. I don't like the way the final project is formatted. The course is okay.

In a class that's fully remote, with no Zoom component to interact with peers, we have TEN group members for our final project. Guess what the project is! It's not a powerpoint. It's not an activity. It's an ESSAY. Just laziness in terms of not wanting to grade individual essays tbh. She makes it so much harder than it has to be.

Will never understand professors like Dionne who want their students to struggle. On top of paying for the textbook, you also have to pay for a discussion board website, despite Canvas having a space for discussions for free. Clearly her real estate business is suffering, otherwise she wouldn't be begging students to follow her Instagram.

analysis.name: Claudia Brosseder
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This professor has an attitude toward her students and her class makes no sense. She treats some students differently and acts like a high school teacher. No one knows how she takes attendance, and you have to Google everything to learn. She makes students present every class, doesn't teach, and even turned off my camera once for no reason.

On the first day of classes when people stated why they were taking her class she got really annoyed when saying it was to fullfill a gen ed. She does not have many assignments just like 4 in class journals that consist of lectures, readings and videos but she is a tough grader. You will lose points if you do not give really specific answers.

Dr. Brosseder is a great professor! I had her for HIST 105 and she was a super engaging lecturer. She grades very reasonably and cares a lot about her students. Honestly as long as you participate and put in a decent amount of effort you should do great!
Pretty easy class, mostly group presentations

Confusing grader- stay after class to discuss assignments.
Teach yourself- review slides with index cards
Was against making outlines for exams??? 
Would forget about assignments posted on the syllabus?
Never told you what to study for exactly 
Easy to talk to
Overall choose another course if not into reading or self teaching yourself

analysis.name: John Claborn
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Claborn is a very nice guy, would definitely take again! RHET105 is composition 1 for the University of Illinois so the curriculum is standardized no matter who teaches it. Hence why it uses an online textbook. My advice: Work a little ahead so the essays are not overwhelming. The essays you write throughout are based on your interests.

he's a great professor, probably one of the nicest professors i've ever had. 

had him for ENGL259 and he very clearly knew what he was talking about.

the class organisation was a little iffy sometimes and he didn't always respond to emails the best, 

but we all (the whole class) LOVED prof claborn he was the best ♡₊˚

He loves his students and he makes all assignments manageable for his students to complete on time. He is really nice and I loved hearing about his personal life. He understands that students are taking difficult classes and that his class isn't probably a priority. Take him if you can. It will be fun and stress free.

I love this man. He is so kind and truly cares about his students. He doesn't make us do busy work assignments, everything he does is for a reason and helps in the long run. We had to write 3 pretty long papers, but he is very gracious and gives valuable feedback to everyone. Definitely recommend!!

John is AMAZING! He is genuinely so caring and wants the best for his students. If you have to take RHET105 at UIUC, then I would more than recommend selecting John as your professor. There are a lot of essays to write but they are all very manageable.

analysis.name: Cliff Shin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Choosing Professor Shin's courses throughout my tenure in the Industrial Design program was one of the best decisions I could make for my skill-building and career. If you pull yourself up by the bootstraps and exceed in design coursework, he will do his best to create opportunities and lay the groundwork for your success. But it depends on you.

One of the most knowledgeable and dedicate professors on the staff. He is consistently pushing his students to do their best. Although the curriculum is demanding at times, what you learn is invaluable and eternally applicable the Industrial Design industry.

The hardest class I've ever taken but overall he's the only tough professor at A+D and will make you work hard for the grade. He can be hard to read as far as banter but just play along. All in all, take Shin at your own risk. If you think your one of the top people in ID take him so you can get humbled.
He is the most reliable and knolwegeable professor in the Industrial Design department at the UIUC. His expectation to students is generally really high, but that makes the work quality a lot higher.

Expect your grade not to reflect the effort you put into the class. Gives poor feedback and is strict about deadlines, but if you ask for help beforehand he will give it.  He's not very clear about expectations, but has very high standards.  Sometimes offensive humor. Expects a lot from students. Would not take another class from him, personally.

analysis.name: Colleen Lewis
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Colleen's class made me reconsider taking more CS courses. The material wasn't very difficult, but lectures were often disorganized and hard to follow. Attendance was emphasized more than clear instruction. Many resources were mentioned, though few were truly helpful for understanding the material. (RMP doesn't support free speech)

Her lectures are pretty much useless, she doesn't talk about what's on the test in lectures, the only reason for my A is self-teaching the material. There is an exam every other week which must be completed outside of normal class time, and she takes attendance in lectures by making all 300+ students scan their ID's before they leave every lecture.

Probably the worst professor at UIUC. Lectures aren't worth anything so get ready to teach yourself everything. She's also really annoying and will say 'Yo' about 99 times a lecture. Take stat 107 this is the worst class ever taught by the worst professor ever.

Worst prof ever. Mandatory lectures and points off for checking your phone. The lecture was not even helpful, and when all the students asked for live coding she did it once and did it wrong. Worst 2 hours of my week.
Yo, so if you're reading this and yo let me tell you you might be the most patient person on earth but, yo, I can't emphasize this enough: Yo gone get sick of the word "yo" if you take this class.

analysis.name: Jacob Covey
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This course tries to convey too much material for one semester. Homework problems are very time consuming, sometimes going up to part (h) for a single problem and are not very instructive. The second exam was also much more difficult than the first exam, leading to a very easy final. If this course cuts down on some material, it can be instructive.

Professor Covey is decent. His lectures are inoffensive but nothing special. You'll do more learning from practice problems and the discussion section anyways. Demos during the lecture are interesting and entertaining. Overall, he conveys the material needed in a clear and concise manner. It's easy to understand.

Does not care about students. He prevented me from accessing study materials for the final because I had to take it late due to illness. Lectures were delivered in the most monotonous way possible and concepts were extremely hard to understand. Steer clear.

Covey is a OK person, but the lecture often leaves with few information or lets you confused. Learn with the TA and be aware of the final exam that worth you 30% of the grade with only about 12 questions.

Covey is a ok to good lecturer. However, good lecturer is not required to do well in the class, as the class mostly consists of conceptually understanding formulas. I learned mostly through my discussion TA and understanding practice tests. 50% of the class is non-exams, so as long as you get above 80s on all the exams you should end up with an A.

analysis.name: Bradley Mehrtens
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 382 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: shawty doesnt even teach he just talks like hes on broadway

I got an A but this class sucked the life out of me. Lectures don't cover the test material and you have to try to learn everything in the textbook on your own. Final exam average was a 54% this year. If you are thinking of taking this class first semester on campus, don't. Nice guy but the worst teacher I have ever had.

Only thing you will learn from Brad's MCB150 is how to google the answers quickly during the quests. You wont learn anything in lecture from those pointless case studies. Brad is an L professor, you only learn in office hours which rarely helps either for the stupid questions on the quest that are every other week smh. would not recommend.

Have never hated a professor more. Brad does not care about students & only wants to perform on stage and brag about his knowledge. Test questions are irrelevant, one-off statements that Brad makes. Tests are so difficult that the averages are never above 70%. Brad is also condescending. The only way to do well is to attend every office hours.

This class is unnecessarily, extremely difficult. Lectures are designed for him to boast knowledge, not teach. It's a 100-level class with 300 level exams. At the beginning of the semester, he'll say, "this class isn't a weed out". Don't listen...it 100% is. Averages are always terrible (60% or below), and discussions are useless and unhelpful.

analysis.name: David Cooper
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
great professor, knows what he's talking about (took ENGL322 (dostoevsky)). very traditionally humanities-style discussion heavy classes. get your readings done. DON'T SKIP YOUR READINGS

doesn't offer any extra credit, very strict with deadlines.
One of the best professors I've ever had. You'll get an A if you keep up with the readings and discussions, and every discussion was very interesting.

Easy course. Just have to hit all the marks on participation and discussion. Easy as long as you put some effort in. He is really nice and wants you to succeed. Beyond helpful. Not the most knowledgeable for the course, but knows enough to get by. Definitely sticks to the material and doesn't stray from presentations.

He is a great professor! Do not be hesitant to ask him for help, because he will gladly assist. His lectures are fun, as he jokes quite often. We did do one rather difficult paper, but he offered extra credit and opportunities to rewrite.

analysis.name: Mary Rose Cottingham
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Mrs. Cottingham is genuinely amazing, and I absolutely loved her class. She gives great feedback on the essays and assignments you submit, and she genuinely cares about her students. The class is a 4-credit-hour class, so it can be a bit tedious at times, but it is still very manageable thanks to Mrs. Cottinham's structure.

Pretty easy English class. Easier than my last high school teacher. Be ready to put work into essays since you will have to write a lot. She allows you to revise papers so this is a pretty easy class to pass. Highly recommend

Mrs. Cottingham is super sweet and genuinely cares about her students. Attendance is mandatory and counts as a grade, but you do not need to pay attention. Everything she discusses is linked in canvas and mentioned in her weekly newsletter. She provides LOTS of feedback on essays. Only downside is all the peer-reviewing required.
Took this class for Advanced Composition. Mrs. Cottingham is very sweet and very passionate about teaching, and will go to great lengths to guide students on the writing assignments.

Mrs. Cottingham is one of the best professors at this university. She is kind and gives great feedback on every essay to ensure you know exactly what to improve on. Her office hours and individual conferences help a ton, as she can break down her feedback for you while you go through your paper, and you can make corrections in front of her as well.

analysis.name: Jesse Couture
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: HK154 is not a class you have to worry about, but Dr. Couture makes it fun with some humor in lecture. Super nice, calm, and approachable guy. It's easy to go up to him after class or email him and ask questions. He has sent me a very detailed email with a nuanced response to one of my questions. Paying attention in lecture is enough to ace tests
Such a good professor, loved the lectures. Easy class with relevant and interesting topics. There were weekly assignments that rarely took longer than 30 minutes.
He is so nice and awesome and the class is very easy

analysis.name: Stephanie Craft
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data
